competency_fulfillment.rationale: No sample asks the student to compare 1/2 to 1/4; seed 42 ("A shape is divided into 2 equal parts. 1 part is shaded. What fraction of the shape is shaded?") only identifies a single fraction, while seeds 44 and 45 ("Compare the numbers: 10 ___ 6. Which sign is correct: >, <, or =?", "Compare the numbers: 18 ___ 30. Which sign is correct: >, <, or =?") compare bare whole numbers with no fraction involved at all.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The one sub-case this competency names, a side-by-side comparison of a half model against a quarter model, is entirely absent across all nine samples.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Seed 50's text ("20 cannot be determined 13. True or False?") is malformed, embedding the phrase 'cannot be determined' as if it were a comparison operator between 20 and 13, producing a sentence a Grade 1 reader cannot parse as a math statement.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: None of the nine samples ever frames a direct 1/2-versus-1/4 comparison; content splits between single-fraction identification and whole-number magnitude comparison, neither of which is the named variant.

competency_alignment.rationale: Seeds 44 and 45 ("Compare the numbers: 10 ___ 6. Which sign is correct: >, <, or =?", "Compare the numbers: 18 ___ 30. Which sign is correct: >, <, or =?") vary along a completely unrelated axis, whole-number magnitude with values like 10, 6, 18, and 30, rather than building the fraction-comparison skill.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Where fractions appear they are correctly restricted to 1/2 and 1/4, but the off-topic whole-number items use unrelated values (6, 10, 18, 30) that never connect back to the fraction pair the competency is scoped to.
